For example, a newly initialized Professor site after the Professor has been killed can still have attendants and regular loot, although its boss spawner is suppressed. A “no boss” room is not automatically an empty POI.

Building4 ItemSpawn_Unique_BossRoom (110836) tests its own OnOff and room Player trigger, with no boss death gate. It iterates its entire ItemSpawnUnique list (ArrayListGetNext endIndex=0 means to end, confirmed installed action code). The list has 36 entries, including sanity pills, three armor plates, multiple Blastlance1/2 instances, four grenades, and ammo stacks. Its consumed flag is independent from the boss. Physical door access can impose the effective encounter ordering without a direct boss-death condition on the loot spawner.

Arena doors

BossDoor is a separate FSM from ItemSpawner. Building4's door listens to Black's global flag; Building6's listens to Professor's; Camp14's listens to Duke's. They continue testing death while waiting/closed and open when it becomes true. Camp14 and Building4 show “A garage door has been opened outside” for eight scaled seconds before their final open-door state. Camp14's initial close-position action is disabled, while other door/motion actions remain active.

Cave5 and Cave6 contain copied BossDoor FSMs (104388,104759) testing the Duke flag despite their actual Alpha/Scorpion spawn gate. Their SetPosition door targets are null in these serialized prefabs. Treat this as an identified prefab oddity; the evidence does not establish a functioning lock whose condition is Duke's death.

Site discovery implementation

Camp10 codex_trigger/codexTrigger (103954) waits for Player OnTriggerEnter, reads __GameManager__.Codex.camp_10, and if already true stops in off. Otherwise it sets camp_10=true and sends the Codex event to the game manager (new-entry toast). The game manager toast is shown four seconds (detail 723–738). This avoids another catalog toast for another Camp10 while leaving its world spawn/contents untouched.

Camp_10 mapIcon/Visited (109192) starts with a one-second allowance for loading, tests its own mapIcon bool, then listens for Player entry into its child trigger; on visit it sets the icon yellow (RGBA approximately .976,1,0,1) and writes mapIcon=true. The icon's separate position-keyed saveItemVar persists its per-site visited state. This change is presentation/discovery bookkeeping; it neither kills enemies nor sets child ItemSpawner.OnOff.

Complete spawner catalog

extracted/spawner-catalog.json contains 219 distinct static ItemSpawner prefab components from sharedassets1.assets, not runtime scene clones. It includes source path and asset ID; enabled/start state; restart/reset flags; random count ranges; distance compares where applicable; Player trigger actions and actual collider volumes; named boss tests; weighted integer selections; resolved ArrayList prefab pools; and enabled/disabled save binding evidence. This includes a few generic unattached template prefabs; actual world-site definitions have Camp_*, Cave_*, Building_*, Wreck_* roots. Preserve that distinction in an HTML catalog.

Weather shell and moving hazard (final supplemental review)

Sandstorm_1 is a stationary graph-generated spawn shell, not the moving weather object. Its child EnemySpawn_Sandstorm/ItemSpawner (sharedassets1.assets:110225) starts in wait, skips if OnOff>0, otherwise waits one scaled second and immediately creates a SandStorm GameObject (prefab9139) from its sole EnemySpawn proxy entry. Despite the child name beginning EnemySpawn, it creates the storm hazard, not a group of mutant NPCs. It has no Player-entry trigger or time-of-day condition. The serialized numberEnd is zero; the loop creates its first storm before comparing number=1 against numberEnd=0, so it stops after one. It registers the moving object in NewGO_ArrayList/ArrayList_Sandstorms, names it with an item ID, then sets OnOff=1. The shell's position-keyed saveItemVar (108771) copies that child OnOff into OnOff_Enemy and restores it on load.

The moving SandStorm/Move FSM (104975) waits one second, turns toward the Player once (LookAt.everyFrame=false, keepVertical=true), draws local-forward velocity z uniformly20–30m/s, and applies that local velocity every frame. It therefore travels along its initial heading; this FSM does not continuously steer to the player. A global LoadVar event selects a separate load state, rerolls velocity20–30, and applies forward velocity without the initial LookAt action. Reload can change storm speed while preserving its restored orientation.

SandStorm/SandPlayer (104015) provides proximity presentation. Below2500m between storm root and Player it enables the Sand Player particle emission and continually puts that child particle object at the Player's position. Above2500m it disables that emission. The strict less/greater compares leave the current state unchanged at exactly2500m. This threshold controls player dust presentation, not creation/destruction of the moving storm. Registered storms are deleted only by the game manager's separate strict>50000m storm cleanup (level1:11866 DeleteFarAwayItems check3/delete3), apart from other explicit destruction such as the disable-storm setting.

The moving prefab carries three tornado physics children. Their TornadoDamage FSMs (107429,110202,110875) handle OnTriggerEnter on layer10 with Bodypart.Damage=-5000 and layer6 with Damage=-5, broadcast Damage to the collided object, then wait0.1s and resume entry detection. These values are action-level damage parameters, not a guaranteed measured health loss. Separate Tornado/Movement FSMs animate and apply tornado physics; they are part of a real moving hazard rather than a texture-only biome effect.

Settings that affect population outside placement

Gameplay_Canvas/.../peaceful_mode/peacefulMode (level1:13695) enables/disables __GameManager__.PeacefulMode (11888). When enabled, the manager waits five scaled seconds, stops boss music/hides boss UI, iterates ArrayList_Items, and destroys each registered object whose current layer equals10. This operates after spawn; the reviewed ItemSpawner/site graph is not conditionally disabled by this setting. A child spawner that already set OnOff=1 is still consumed when its actor is subsequently destroyed, and switching peaceful mode off does not reset that flag or restore the actor.

The disable-storm toggle (13542) similarly enables/disables __GameManager__.DisableSandstorm (11891), a five-second periodic ArrayList_Sandstorms sweep destroying objects whose layer equals2. It does not suppress Sandstorm_1 generation or restore a consumed storm-shell flag. The manager FSM is disabled by default in the serialized normal scene; the gameplay setting toggles its enabled state.

No day/night or difficulty check was found in the219 static ItemSpawner prefab FSMs. A Wreck_7 wild spawner, for example, randomly chooses its Mutant versus Carnivore branch (enemyType inclusive random0–1), rather than reading DayTime. Catalog8092 contains only a game-manager FSM named DayTime, not a distinct night/day spawn controller. This does not assert that darkness has no effect on other visual or NPC behavior; it specifically rules out a day/night spawn gate in the reviewed world-content spawners. Weather supplemental source is extracted/weather-fsm.json, merged into decoded-fsm.json; every item above gives a static source ID.

Persistence and cleanup review — source references and exact fields

Persistence, respawn, despawn, merchants (source audit, 4 October 2026)

Primary evidence is decoded vanilla assets in persistence-fsm.txt, cleanup-fsm.txt, save-trigger-fsm.txt, merchant-stock-fsm.txt. These are offline decodes of Unity assets, not modified FSMs. The two existing BepInEx dumps are live snapshots and may differ in runtime variables because a saved character and mods were active. Position-dependent cases require controlled gameplay verification; the code does not expose one universal timed camp respawn rule.

Direct answers and the required distinctions

Discovering is not the same as spawning, killing, or clearing. mapIcon/Visited starts with a one-second wait, reads its Boolean mapIcon, and listens for Player entering its own child trigger. A successful entry changes the icon color and sets mapIcon=true; it does not reset ItemSpawner.OnOff and does not declare the whole camp cleared. See persistence-fsm.txt:559-571, live Camp10 fsm_dump.txt:7828-7861. Camp enemies, critters, sale stock, loot and vehicles have separate spawner flags and trigger volumes. It is possible to see/visit a POI while a particular spawn volume was never crossed.

The usual spawner is one-shot per retained/restored flag. ItemSpawner starts in wait. Every frame, OnOff>0 sends it straight to spawned; otherwise after one game-time second it arms the Player-entry trigger. Once its batch is completed, spawned sets OnOff=1 and has no exit or periodic timer. Re-enabling the FSM restarts at wait but ResetVariablesOnEnable=0, so existing OnOff survives. See persistence-fsm.txt:319-349 (critter), 351-387 (Coyote enemies), 389-427 (ordinary loot), 521-557 (cars). No DayChanged or calendar respawn transition exists in these FSMs. Enemy death does not itself run the parent spawner again.

Going farther than 5 km destroys tracked objects, not their spawner flag. The global deletion loop destroys registered Items and Cars using each object's distance to Player. It never sets its source camp's OnOff back to zero. Consequently, if the same POI instance remains in the terrain pool, returning finds that spawn category empty after its objects have been deleted. It is still the same recognizable camp/building and may have other untouched static objects or untriggered categories. This is the precise empty-camp failure mode; 5 km is not a camp refresh threshold.

A universal claim that the camp stays empty forever is also unsupported. Tile streaming can retain, recycle or destroy static POI instances. If a fresh POI object is created with default OnOff=0, it can spawn another batch on entry unless a Load event restores its position-keyed flags (and, for bosses, the global killed flag can separately veto it). Conversely, pooled instances keep their existing variables, even if repositioned by list index. See terrain findings. The native save/load coordinator only finds currently active SpawnerStatic objects for restoration. Ordinary spawners do not self-load their saved record when they are enabled later. Thus same-instance revisiting, reloading near a saved POI, and arriving later at a newly regenerated POI are distinct paths; no code-supported fixed number of days guarantees repopulation.

Dynamic objects: the complete global cleanup table

Path Criteria Operation Return behavior
Registered ArrayList_Items Distance >1,000 m; not layer22 SetActive(false), about every5 game-time seconds Same surviving object is SetActive(true) below1,000m. It is not regenerated and variable reset depends on its FSM flags.
Registered ArrayList_Items Layer22 Force active in activation pass; exempt distance deletion Preserve object while registered. Do not label every possible inventory/held item exempt without inspecting its current layer.
Registered ArrayList_Items Distance >5,000m; not layer22 DestroyObject; no detached children Gone from the current live world. No camp flag reset.
Registered ArrayList_Cars Distance >5,000m DestroyObject; no layer exemption Car and its descendants are gone. This includes cars left behind; no vanilla ownership exemption appears here.

Evidence: cleanup-fsm.txt:1-32, 34-51, 53-72, 84-98; live detailed values fsm_detail.txt:842-1122. Deletion scans wait10 game-time seconds between list sweeps. Thresholds are strict greater-than for distance; exactly1,000 or5,000 has no new comparison event. Distances come from GetDistance between GameObjects (Euclidean3D), not traveled-road length. The inactive loop has disabled SetIsKinematic actions: do not describe vanilla distance sleep as changing Rigidbody.isKinematic.

NewGO_ArrayList/DeleteDestroyedItems regularly removes Unity-null references from Items/Cars/Sandstorms, not a permanent world respawn ledger (persistence-fsm.txt:257-284, live fsm_dump.txt:29405-29430). Saved object arrays represent the objects still registered at save time. Saving after destruction cannot restore the deleted live object as though it had merely been hidden. Loading an older save taken before destruction can restore the older object population.

How local spawn batches actually work

Ordinary ItemSpawner trigger rolls numberEnd using RandomInt, waits for Player entry, then chooses an item index using SelectRandomInt relative weights and gets the prefab from an ArrayList. Loot uses the global NewGO_ArrayList ItemList; authored enemy/critter spawners use an EnemySpawn list on the spawner. CarSpawn uses ArrayListGetRandom on its CarSpawn list. Every prefab selection uses runtime Unity random, independently of deterministic MapMagic terrain coordinates; the static site can be repeatable while its dynamic batch varies.

Spawn location comes either from the spawner's own transform or successive children of its next sibling spawn_locations group (GetGameObjectSibling(index=1) then GetNextChild). Created objects ordinarily have no parent assigned; they become dynamic roots rather than remaining children of the static site. Apply random yaw; tell itemNameID FSM Activate to increment the persistent ID; read intName; append it to the instantiated name; add the clone to ArrayListItems (loot, NPCs, critters, merchants) or ArrayListCars (cars); optionally send Randomize or ForBuy to initialize object state. Object-specific randomizers can choose condition, fluid contents and gear; the local spawner marks the batch complete afterward. See persistence-fsm.txt:328-339, 365-377, 405-417, 537-548; mod equivalent used for corroboration Apocaspawner/Spawner.cs:352-378.

Counts are authored per prefab and sometimes overwritten by its ItemNum FSM. Example Coyote spawner decoded here rolls3-4; ordinary critter spawner rolls0-2 but the graph always executes getItem/spawn at least once before checking count, so a zero result does not necessarily produce zero creatures (persistence-fsm.txt:325-349). Do not turn these counts into universal game-wide values. Each POI may contain multiple independent spawners, including boss, guards, raids, crates, unique item and ordinary enemies.

The ordinary loot table example contains272 indexed options and explicit relative weights, including very small weights for rare entries. The arrays are in persistence-fsm.txt:427; they are weights normalized by selection, not literal spawn percentages. Merchant stock uses ArrayListGetRandomCurvedWeighted (merchant-stock-fsm.txt:33-36) rather than the disabled legacy SelectRandomInt table. The stock spawner uses ForBuy instead of ordinary Randomize; a liquid stock spawner explicitly creates GasolineCan, DieselCan and WaterCanPlastic, registers them and marks OnOff=1 (persistence-fsm.txt:470-519). Merely having minItemNum/maxItemNum variables in that FSM does not imply it rolls that many cans: its active states create exactly these three.

What saves retain and what they do not

The save button activates every registered Item before saving (save-trigger-fsm.txt:30-40, cleanup-fsm.txt:74-82). This permits normally inactive objects and their FSMs to participate in saving. It then sends SaveGame to SaveLoadGame, NewGOArrayList, Player, PlayerCameraHolder, StarterArea, GameManager, itemNameID. NewGO resizes its snapshot arrays, finds active objects tagged SpawnerStatic, collects and sends SaveGame to dynamic objects and their children, sends Save to static objects and their children, stores arrays for cars/items/sandstorms, and writes the cached files (persistence-fsm.txt:167-256).

Static Camp10 saveItemVar uses its world position as save key. It snapshots five distinct values: Critter, Merchant, Merchant_Item, Enemy, MerchantLiquids OnOff. On Load it reads the record and restores each corresponding child FSM integer (persistence-fsm.txt:1-25). Other POIs save different lists; Cave7 live example has distinct boss/bodyguard/enemy/unique-item flags (fsm_dump.txt:24901-24920). Do not infer a universal single Visited/cleared bool from these data.

Load reconstructs terrain using the saved graph seed and MapMagic position, waits for generation, restores dynamic object arrays and variables, finds currently active SpawnerStatic objects and sends Load to restore their flags, then finishes the loading UI. SaveAll saves named FSM variables, not the current FSM state; saved OnOff is what suppresses a fresh batch. Native active-only lookup comes directly from GameObject.FindGameObjectsWithTag in persistence-code/HutongGames.PlayMaker.Actions.ArrayListFindGameObjectsByTag.decompiled.cs:38-44.

EasySave action paths shown in dumps are often editor defaults. If overrideDefaultSettings=false, SettingsAction.GetSettings uses global ES3Settings instead of the displayed path/location. Slot buttons call ES3SettingsMod.SetSavePath and update SaveNewGOArrayList.SaveFile. Avoid saying all data writes to literal SaveFile.es3 just because the SaveAll action inspector displays it (persistence-code/ES3PlayMaker.SettingsAction.decompiled.cs:74-93, live fsm_detail.txt:58761-58772).

Merchant refresh: three separate systems

  1. Physical merchant NPC: one-shot merchant spawn OnOff, tracked as a dynamic Item. Can be hidden/deleted by the Item cleanup and will not be replenished by a retained OnOff=1 spawner.
  2. Physical goods sold to the player: one-shot stock and liquid spawners, tracked dynamic Items with ForBuy status. Selling/buying/5km destruction does not reset the stock spawner. Existing surviving goods are serialized as objects, so loading does not intentionally restock a recorded OnOff=1 camp.
  3. Wanted goods purchased from player: Sell_Items/ItemList is a static child and separate generator, with no OnOff and no Save or SaveGame transitions. It waits until Player is <500m away, rolls8-10 rows in the decoded standard version, chooses candidates from ItemBuySellList using a weight curve, temporarily creates each prefab to query ItemName and SellValue, writes the names and prices to arrays/text labels, then destroys the temporary candidate objects. See persistence-fsm.txt:27-81.

The audited code confirms randomized wanted lists on a fresh load/recreated merchant site; it does not confirm an immediate nearby-merchant wanted-list reroll from merely saving. Native save activates ArrayListItems. Static SellItems is never registered in that list by its generator, and native SaveGame/Save targets have no transition that restarts ItemList. A save followed by reload naturally rebuilds these unsaved lists, so that observed behavior should be named save-and-reload refresh. Save can wake far-away dynamic goods/NPCs as a side effect, but this does not establish wanted-list reroll. There is no inspected daily refresh timer here.

Reactivating the same static Sell_Items FSM is a separate edge case: RestartOnEnable=1, ResetVariablesOnEnable=0 means number, arrays and child iteration counters persist. The states have no explicit ArrayClear/number=0 before generation. It may append/rewrite rows rather than produce a clean full refresh; fresh-instance reload is the reliable reroll path. The weighted action declares repeat=false but its decompiled GetRandomItem never reads repeat, so duplicates are not proven excluded.

Installed mods and repository defaults (separate from vanilla)

  • Apocasaver autosaves via the native savegame FSM, so it inherits its activation/persistence side effects. Source default interval10min; current installed config is enabled with interval30min (Apocasaver/Plugin.cs:61-66, :134-190, installed config lines20/33). Its held-item fixes make saves safer but do not create camp restocking or POI respawn.
  • Apocapatrol has additional cleanup for its own raider vehicles: defaults MinDistance800m, RemoveAfterMinutes10, MaxCars30. It excludes cars ever occupied by Player from its own cleanup; vanilla5km cleanup remains a distinct path. Apocapatrol/Cleanup.cs:32-94, Plugin.cs:413-420. Its persistence companion file saves patrol state in addition to native registered cars; no change to base world geography.
  • Apocatremors adds moving-player ambushes and destroys its tracked spawned creatures beyond configured DespawnDistance (source default300m). This can explain disappearances far below vanilla5km. Apocatremors/Tremors.cs:209-222, Plugin.cs:88-90.
  • Apocaspawner-created objects increment the same itemNameID and enter Items/Cars tracking, so ordinary save/despawn rules apply (Spawner.cs:352-378). It does not create a repeatable camp spawn trigger.

Evidence limits and useful verification cases

This audit establishes code paths and static asset configuration; it does not execute irreversible gameplay or write saves. Claims needing a controlled throwaway save include: same-site unload/reload after long travel; fresh instance creation vs pool reuse; sites first generated after the load coordinator's SpawnerStatic scan; save-only demand refresh with Player staying nearby; re-enabling same static merchant arrays; and objects protected by current layer22. These limits should accompany the confident empty-camp answer rather than be hidden.

Followup: exactly what sets loot counts and the starter economy

All50 decoded ItemNum FSMs (including live scene duplicates) are constant author overrides: one enabled state runs exactly two SetFsmInt actions, writing minItemNum and maxItemNum to the same object's ItemSpawner, everyFrame=false. They contain no difficulty, travel-distance, boss-count or loot-multiplier calculation. Searching the whole decoded1996-FSM set found no min/max SetFsmInt writers outside these ItemNum components. ItemSpawner.RandomInt then uses these limits with inclusiveMax=true. Source: item-counts-and-starter.txt:1-50; raw decoded metadata in item-counts-and-starter.json.

The ranges below are per spawner component, not the sum of all contents in a camp or multi-level site. A site with an underground area has a separate batch and its own flag there. Standalone rows are prefab defaults; containing POIs can override them. These are physical loot and physical sale stock, not merchant wanted-list size.

Starter car, matching parts, supplies

The starting area uses deliberately generous automatic initialization instead of ordinary Player-entry loot batches. These spawners all keep OnOff one-shot guards and register spawned objects in the same native dynamic lists.

  • CarSpawnStarterBase waits0.2 game-time seconds, chooses uniformly from its six-entry CarSpawn list, creates it at the spawner with configured rotation(0,90,0), registers in ArrayListCars, sends Randomize, waits0.2s and adds15 to the current fuel object's Liquid. It creates one car. It does not wait for a Player trigger. Choices in list/index order: Poloska, Junker, PipeRat, Crossbreed, TinyTyrant, Halfbreed. Source: item-counts-and-starter.txt:207-229; list extracted/level1-13618-PlayMakerArrayListProxy.json:27-59.
  • EngineSpawn_StarterBase waits0.3s, reads that car spawner's chosen index and creates compatible parts. Poloska/PipeRat/TinyTyrant get594cc I2 gasoline engine plus motorcycle radiator; Junker gets1.2L I4 gasoline engine plus small radiator; Crossbreed/Halfbreed get594cc engine plus two motorcycle wheels. Each part is named/registered, receives Randomize, waits0.2s, then the starter helper adds5 to Liquid and50 to Condition and attempts1.5 to a cap tagged MotorOil. These are additions to existing randomized values, not promises that final condition or contents equal those numbers. Radiator/wheel helpers repeat the same cap lookup pattern; do not promise oil is a valid field on every part. Source: item-counts-and-starter.txt:52-177 (all branch/state actions).
  • ItemSpawnStarterBase waits0.25s and iterates the entire fixed22-entry ItemSpawnStarterBase list in order. It assigns each to the next child spawn position, randomizes all three rotation axes, registers it, sends Randomize, waits0.1s, then adds8 to Liquid,40 to Condition, attempts3 to a MotorOil cap and4 to a Water cap before advancing. It does not roll a random count or random selection from that list. Source: item-counts-and-starter.txt:179-205; extracted/level1-12973-PlayMakerArrayListProxy.json holds the actual22 entries.

Fixed starting supplies, in order: dogfoodcan; gaugeoiltemp; poloskaexhaust; Headlight; MotorOilCanSmall; smallwheel1; smallwheel2; WaterCanPlastic; poloskasteeringwheel1; poloskagearlever1; tincanlight; cassette80ssynthwave; bandage1; radiocar; a second smallwheel1; smallwheel3; RepairboxMedium; Toolbox; poloskaseatfronthomemade; GasolineCan; gauge_speedo; shiv. These supplies remain fixed even when the randomly selected car is another of the six chassis, while the separate engine/part branch adapts to it.

Starter CritterSpawn still uses the ordinary Player-entry0–2 target-count graph and0/1/2 do-while caveat, with OnOff guard; it is not part of the22-list. Source: item-counts-and-starter.txt:231-257.

Complete extracted spawner catalogue — 219 prefab definitions

These are serialized static prefab definitions, including some generic unattached templates. World-site definitions have Camp_, Cave_, Building_ or Wreck_ roots. Individual records preserve count actions, room volumes, weighted pools, saved-flag bindings and enabled fields. A variable reference or stored range alone must be read together with the active FSM loop.

Primary evidence:

  • Unity packed files level1, sharedassets1.assets, resources.assets, globalgamemanagers.assets and sharedassets0.assets, extracted read-only from data.unity3d.
  • MyDesert Graph: sharedassets1.assets, object path ID 103111, 140 enabled generator nodes. Manually decoded with regenerated type trees; 208,692 of 208,692 raw bytes consumed.
  • Scene MapMagicObject: level1, object path ID 11687, 616 of 616 raw bytes consumed.
  • Active NWH FloatingOrigin: level1, object path ID 13495.
  • PlayMaker: offline parsed FSMs plus a lightweight catalogue of 8,092 serialized FSM definitions across scene/prefabs. The selected detailed extraction includes world, population, boss, merchant, codex, site-root and save FSMs; framework action code resolves weighting, serialization and active-only lookup behavior.
  • Existing BepInEx/fsm_dump.txt and fsm_detail.txt, inspector snapshots dated 1 October 2026. Runtime values represent that character/session and can differ from authored defaults.
  • Title-menu level0: 37 menu FSMs, including NewGame/GetSeed, plus the authored seed InputField. See research/menu-fsm.txt and research/extracted/menu-seed-inputfield.json.
  • Decompiled managed MapMagic, Den.Tools, PlayMaker and ES3 actions in the research folder. Object names alone were not accepted as proof of actual action targets: the Cave_7 copied local Boss_Duke_Ironjaw name, for example, does not override its actual global Terror-of-the-Night check.

Source navigation:

  • research/terrain.md, research/graph-summary.txt, decoded Graph/MapMagicObject JSON and research/terrain-code/.
  • research/encounters.md, research/encounter-fsm.txt, resolved boss-site table and extracted spawner catalogue.
  • research/persistence.md, research/persistence-fsm.txt, research/cleanup-fsm.txt, research/save-trigger-fsm.txt, research/merchant-stock-fsm.txt and research/persistence-code/.

Reproduce the reader document with python build_document.py from this output folder after installing markdown2. Extraction helpers require UnityPy and TypeTreeGeneratorAPI. They read game assets and write only task-owned research outputs. The HTML itself has no external dependencies.

Known interpretation limits: runtime route-specific pool identity, event ordering for already armed boss spawners, later generation outside the active load sweep, and same-instance merchant reactivation. The document explicitly distinguishes those from direct serialized values and executable cleanup checks.

Offline document. All styling, diagrams, interaction and source notes are included in this file. No game files or saves were changed during the review.
